newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees HUF 1800bln '97 govt securities issues.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees HUF 1800bln '97 govt securities issues.

text.p: Hungary plans to increase the total amount of government securities issues to some 1,800 billion forints in 1997 from 1,430 billion forints in 1996, the Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) said on Thursday.
The net financing requirement of the state treasury would be around 360 billion forints this year, up from 199 bilion forints in 1996, AKK Director Zsuzsa Acs told a news conference.

The main cause of the increase would be the widening of the central state budget deficit to 360 billion forints in 1997 from some 130 billion forints in 1996, due to technical changes in the accounting of the foreign state debt, AKK officials said. These figures exclude privatisation revenues.
AKK expects interest rate trends to remain favourable for the state as a borrower this year and sees last year's dramatic fall continuing at a slower pace.
Twelve-month Treasury bill yields have dropped some ten percentage points since the end of 1995 to 20.85 percent.

"The success of the new five-year bonds last week have also showed that we are going in the right direction and the market accepts our expectations (of the decline of inflation)," said finance ministry deputy secretary of state Csaba Laszlo.
A five-billion forint worth offer of five-year bonds, auctioned the first time ever last week, was six times oversubscribed, with the average yield set at 15.69 percent.
Hungary reduced inflation to 23.5 percent last year from 28.2 percent in 1995, and targets some 17 percent for 1997 and 12 percent or even lower levels for 1998.
Expectations of falling inflation enables AKK to lengthen the average maturity of the new securities issues, reducing its short-term interest payment obligations, Acs said.

AKK introduced seven-year and five-year bonds recently and would like to increase the amount of government bond issues to some 550 billion forints this year, Acs said, from 321 billion forints in 1996.
The central state budget's gross domestic debt totalled 4,938 billion forints at the end of 1996, up 224 billion forints from 1995.
